title: Units and locality of an integralized local Kummer pushout
statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be fine saturated commutative monoids, written additively, with group completion as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. For $L=A,B,C$ put $U_L=\{l\in L:-l\in L\}\subset L^{\rm gp}$, its subgroup of units, and $\overline L=L/U_L$, the quotient identifying elements whose difference belongs to $U_L$. Let $f:A\to B$ and $g:A\to C$ be local homomorphisms, meaning $f^{-1}(U_B)=U_A=g^{-1}(U_C)$. Suppose the induced $\overline f:\overline A\to\overline B$ is injective and every $\bar b\in\overline B$ satisfies $n\bar b=\overline f(\bar a)$ for some integer $n>0$ and $\bar a\in\overline A$. Form the abelian group
$$H=(B^{\rm gp}\oplus C^{\rm gp})/\{(f^{\rm gp}(a),-g^{\rm gp}(a)):a\in A^{\rm gp}\},$$
and write $i_B,i_C$ for its canonical maps. Put $M=\{i_B(b)+i_C(c):b\in B,c\in C\}\subset H$ and $U=i_B(U_B)+i_C(U_C)\subset H$. Then the group of units of the integral monoid $M$ is exactly $M\cap(-M)=U$. Moreover, for every $b\in B$ and $c\in C$,
$$i_B(b)\in U\ \Longleftrightarrow\ b\in U_B,\qquad i_C(c)\in U\ \Longleftrightarrow\ c\in U_C.$$

source.place: VI 2.1, printed p.71 (Kummer condition); VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98 (sharpening and localization). Agent-formulated algebraic lemma for the nonemptiness assertion in X 1.8, pp.146--147; not asserted verbatim in ILO. Complete proof in the delivery report. WANTED a direct published reference for local Kummer pushout units.

proof.text: We first analyze a zero relation $i_B(b)+i_C(c)=0$ with $b\in B,c\in C$. The subgroup divided out in the definition of $H$ is the image of $a\mapsto(f^{\rm gp}(a),-g^{\rm gp}(a))$. Thus $(b,c)=(f^{\rm gp}(a),-g^{\rm gp}(a))$ for some $a\in A^{\rm gp}$. By the group-completion presentation in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], write $a=x-y$ with $x,y\in A$ (collect the positive and negative generators). Integrality lets us read the resulting equalities as $f(x)=b+f(y)$ and $g(y)=c+g(x)$ in the monoids.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98 and 3.1.5, p.99. Explicit algebraic argument by the worker, not a quoted theorem.

proof.text: Apply the assumed root-cofinal condition to $\bar b$. Choose $n>0,z\in A,u\in U_B$ with $nb=f(z)+u$. The first equality of Step 1 yields $f(nx)=f(z+ny)+u$. Passing to $\overline B$ and using injectivity of $\overline f$ gives $\overline{nx}=\overline{z+ny}$ in $\overline A$. By the definition of this quotient, $nx=z+ny+v$ in $A^{\rm gp}$ for some $v\in U_A$. Hence $na=z+v$.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98 and 3.1.5, p.99. Explicit algebraic argument by the worker, not a quoted theorem.

proof.text: Apply $g^{\rm gp}$ to $na=z+v$ and use $c=-g^{\rm gp}(a)$ from Step 1. This gives $nc+g(z)=-g(v)$. Both $g(v)$ and $-g(v)=g(-v)$ belong to $C$. The displayed identity gives an inverse $nc+g(v)\in C$ for $g(z)$, and an inverse $g(z)+g(v)\in C$ for $nc$. Consequently $g(z)\in U_C$, so locality of $g$ gives $z\in U_A$.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98 and 3.1.5, p.99. Explicit algebraic argument by the worker, not a quoted theorem.

proof.text: Now $nb=f(z)+u$ is a unit of $B$, with inverse $-f(z)-u=f(-z)-u\in B$. Thus $-b=(n-1)b-f(z)-u\in B$, so $b\in U_B$. Likewise $-c=(n-1)c+g(z)+g(v)\in C$, so $c\in U_C$. This proves that both components of every zero relation considered in Step 1 are units. All inverse formulas are valid also when $n=1$.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98 and 3.1.5, p.99. Explicit algebraic argument by the worker, not a quoted theorem.

proof.text: Let $m=i_B(b)+i_C(c)\in M\cap(-M)$. Write $-m=i_B(b\prime)+i_C(c\prime)$ with $b\prime\in B,c\prime\in C$. Apply Steps 1--4 to $(b+b\prime,c+c\prime)$: both sums are units. Then $-b=b\prime-(b+b\prime)\in B$ and $-c=c\prime-(c+c\prime)\in C$. Thus $b,c$ are units and $m\in U$. Conversely, if $u_B\in U_B,u_C\in U_C$, both $i_B(u_B)+i_C(u_C)$ and its negative $i_B(-u_B)+i_C(-u_C)$ lie in $M$. Therefore $M\cap(-M)=U$.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98 and 3.1.5, p.99. Explicit algebraic argument by the worker, not a quoted theorem.

proof.text: For $i_B(b)\in U$, the equality just proved puts $i_B(b)$ in $M\cap(-M)$. The argument in Step 5 applied to its representation $(b,0)$ gives $b\in U_B$. Conversely $b\in U_B$ implies $i_B(b)\in U$ by its definition. Applying the same argument to the representation $(0,c)$ proves $i_C(c)\in U\Longleftrightarrow c\in U_C$. Finally $M$ is an integral commutative monoid because it is a submonoid of the abelian group $H$; cancellation follows by adding the negative of the common summand.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98 and 3.1.5, p.99. Explicit algebraic argument by the worker, not a quoted theorem.
